## Sampling diagnostics for each model of record {#sec-appendix-b1}

Every model of record is held to the two-tier convergence gate described in
@sec-convergence. The **hard tier** — $\hat{R} \le 1.01$ and effective sample size
$\ge 400$ on every parameter — is fail-closed: no fit that misses it is summarised,
syndicated or published. The **soft tier** — no divergent transitions, and an energy
BFMI $\ge 0.3$ on every chain — is recorded rather than enforced, because for
several models in this family it has not been removable by longer tuning without an
infeasible reparameterisation.

The table below is generated from each fit's own diagnostics payload, so it reports
what the sampler achieved rather than what was intended.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-appendix-convergence
#| tbl-cap: "Achieved sampling diagnostics for every model of record. Divergences and minimum BFMI are the soft tier; max R-hat and min ESS are the hard tier, which every listed fit cleared."
#| echo: false
import pandas as pd

# Generated by scripts/sync_report_figures.py. Read as CSV rather than from each
# fit's diagnostics_summary.json because the figure cache syncs only figures and
# summary tables, so a JSON reader here would render "pending" indefinitely.
_diag_path = FIG_ROOT / "convergence_diagnostics.csv"
_diag = pd.read_csv(_diag_path) if _diag_path.exists() else None
if _diag is not None:
    _diag = (
        _diag.rename(columns={
            "model": "Model", "divergences": "Divergences", "max_rhat": "Max R-hat",
            "min_ess": "Min ESS", "min_bfmi": "Min BFMI",
            "soft_caveats": "Soft-tier caveat",
        })
        .assign(**{"Soft-tier caveat": lambda d: d["Soft-tier caveat"].fillna("").replace("", "—")})
        .style.format({"Max R-hat": "{:.4f}", "Min ESS": "{:,.0f}", "Min BFMI": "{:.3f}"})
        .hide(axis="index")
    )

_show_or_pending(_diag, "the per-model sampling diagnostics")
```

### Fits carrying soft-tier caveats {#sec-appendix-b1-caveats}

The entries below are generated at figure-synchronisation time from the fits
themselves. Where this section reports no caveats, every model of record cleared
both tiers.

A soft-tier caveat bears on **how far into the posterior's tails the sampler
reached**. It therefore qualifies the reported *interval bounds* considerably more
than the *point estimates*: a median or expected count from a caveated fit is
substantially more trustworthy than the edges of its 89% interval. Reported
intervals for these models should be read as indicative rather than exact.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-appendix-caveats
#| tbl-cap: "Soft-tier convergence caveats carried by models of record, as recorded when report figures were synchronised."
#| echo: false
from IPython.display import Markdown

_caveat_path = FIG_ROOT / "convergence_caveats.csv"
_caveats = pd.read_csv(_caveat_path) if _caveat_path.exists() else None

if _caveats is None:
    _out = _show_or_pending(None, "the soft-tier convergence caveats")
elif _caveats.empty:
    # An empty table is a result, not a missing artefact: every model cleared both tiers.
    _out = Markdown("Every model of record cleared both convergence tiers; no fit carries a soft-tier caveat.")
else:
    _out = (
        _caveats.rename(columns={
            "model": "Model", "caveat": "Caveat", "consequence": "Consequence",
        })
        .style.hide(axis="index")
    )
_out
```

## Model specifications

The full specification of each model — its priors, mean-function anchors, dispersion
parameterisation, random-effect structure and sampled quantities — is recorded in that
model's own report under `docs/models/`, and in the registered definition its fit
manifest reproduces verbatim. Consolidating those specifications into this appendix is
outstanding.
